rules.instruction: When the description states one step that can be carried out in one of several named ways, joined by 'or' within the same clause, and the step is followed by a later step that depends on which way was chosen: Model each named way of carrying out the step as its own task. Place an exclusive gateway split before these tasks, with a labeled outgoing flow to each task. Join the alternative tasks with an exclusive gateway merge before the next step. Do not collapse the alternatives into one generic task, and do not keep only one of the named alternatives.
rules.situation: the description states one step that can be carried out in one of several named ways, joined by 'or' within the same clause, and the step is followed by a later step that depends on which way was chosen

rules.instruction: When the description names two or more alternative ways of signalling or performing the same need, where each alternative is a distinct action by a different actor or mechanism, and the alternatives must converge before the next step: Model each alternative as its own activity of the appropriate type on a separate outgoing branch of one exclusive gateway, then rejoin those branches with an exclusive merge before the next decision or step. Do not drop an alternative, and do not connect the gateway directly to the following step when an alternative is described as an action.
rules.situation: the description names two or more alternative ways of signalling or performing the same need, where each alternative is a distinct action by a different actor or mechanism, and the alternatives must converge before the next step

rules.instruction: When the description gives two alternative ways of signalling the same need, one carried out by a mechanism and one carried out by a person, and the person-performed alternative is worded as a check or inspection while the outcome is attributed to that alternative as the way the need is delivered: Model the person-performed alternative as a task whose label names the act that delivers the outcome the description attributes to that alternative, not the verification act that precedes it. Keep it on its own branch, distinct from the mechanism-performed task, so that each alternative's label matches the step the description assigns to it.
rules.situation: the description gives two alternative ways of signalling the same need, one carried out by a mechanism and one carried out by a person, and the person-performed alternative is worded as a check or inspection while the outcome is attributed to that alternative as the way the need is delivered
